summary: Swept model width/depth for the fixed 5-minute budget, holding the optimizer and architecture fixed. Increasing width from the baseline 512 (DEPTH=8) to 640 by raising ASPECT_RATIO to 80 (still DEPTH=8) gave the best result, 0.996232 vs baseline 1.012347. Interestingly, at the same width=640, fewer layers won: DEPTH=8 (0.996232) beat DEPTH=9 (0.998370) and DEPTH=10 (1.001260), showing the earlier depth-increase gains were actually a width effect, not a depth effect, since ASPECT_RATIO=64 rounds width up in steps of HEAD_DIM=128. DEPTH=6 (narrower, more steps) and DEPTH=12 (deeper, OOMs at batch 128) were both worse. Next I would try widening further at DEPTH=8 (ASPECT_RATIO 96-128) and re-tuning LR/batch size for the new width, since LR is already scaled by 1/sqrt(dim/768) but batch/depth interactions weren't explored.
